target_customer: Consumers who buy shampoo, conditioner and later body and skin care and want a formula made for their own hair type and goals; later also mass retail shoppers
problem: Off the shelf hair care is one size fits all, so people with specific hair types, damage or goals buy products that do not suit them.
business_model: Direct to consumer made to order products sold by one time purchase or subscription, later with retail distribution
product_category: Personalized hair, body and skin care

founders.name: Zahir Dossa
education: MIT (per YC company page, which calls him an engineer and MIT graduate)
founders.background_notes: Prior employers not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Hien Kaplan
founders.background_notes: YC page describes her as a cosmetic chemist. Beauty Independent in Dec 2020 calls her CSO.

technical_complexity.rationale: A quiz driven formulation algorithm plus made to order manufacturing and fulfillment was standard software with a hard operations side. TechCrunch in 2017 cites up to 12 billion custom combinations; the company later built its own production facilities in Michigan and Pennsylvania.

defensibility.rationale: The quiz and formulas could be copied, as Prose later showed. Defensibility came from the vertically integrated factory and customer data, which became relevant only after the Series B.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Beauty Independent in Dec 2020 notes that large players moved into personalization later (Unilever Skinsei in 2019, Henkel stake in E-Salon, L'Oreal Color and Co). None had bought the company as of the sources reviewed.

market_need_then: Hair care buyers were already ordering online and a wave of direct to consumer brands existed by 2016. The company claims demand for customized formulas; independent evidence of pain at founding was not found in the sources reviewed.

branding.domain_note: Uses functionofbeauty.com, a full descriptive .com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: A stylized letter F mark (per a 2023 agency case study seen in search results)
identity.visual_style: Clean, bright and approachable, with a brand blue; hair type based shopping
identity.voice_and_tone: Upbeat, playful and approachable; the quiz is framed with a Wizard of Oz reference on the company site

branding.brand_signature: The personalized quiz that names your formula and puts your first name on the bottle (name on bottle not confirmed in sources, so the quiz itself is the signature)
branding.community_and_virality: Many third party review and comparison articles exist against Prose, which shows consumer talk, but no merch or fan community was found.

brand_strength.rationale: Became a widely compared category name in custom hair care with national retail distribution (Target, Sephora per a 2023 agency case study seen in search), but no source shows the brand itself as the main growth driver.

pivots.to: Added customized body care (July 2020) and skin care (October 2020)
pivots.why: Product line expansion reported by Beauty Independent; this is an extension, not a change of market.

outcome_analysis: Function of Beauty raised a $9.5M Series A in 2017 and a $150M Series B led by L Catterton in December 2020 after reported sales growth above 100 percent in 2020 and roughly 400 staff. It built its own factories and expanded from hair into body and skin care and later into physical retail. The company is still active and independent in the sources reviewed, with the main open risks being copycat personalization rivals such as Prose and large incumbents entering the space.
notes: Series A is stated as 9M in the TechCrunch headline and 9.5M in its body and in BeautyMatter and Cooley coverage; 9.5M used. Beauty Independent says the Series A valued the company above 110M, not recorded as post money because the figure is secondhand. Aggregators list a 2016 seed and a possible 2021 or 2022 round; not recorded because only aggregators were seen. Totals disagree across aggregators (164.7M at one, 247.9M at another); disclosed equity per Beauty Independent is 12M Series A plus 150M Series B. The company also raised undisclosed debt. YC page lists three founders; Hien Kaplan is also called Hien Nguyen in the founders narrative. Competitors list left empty: the 2017 TechCrunch article names none and sources naming rivals (Prose, Unilever, Henkel, L'Oreal) are dated 2019 or later, so they are not used as of founding.
